newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open stronger amid dollar gains.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open stronger amid dollar gains.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened stronger on Wednesday amid strength in the currency, with the market benefiting further from Tuesday's decision by the U.S. Federal Reserve to hold rates steady, dealers said.

"When the Fed didn't move yesterday, that was just the trigger that was needed to rally the market and the currency, and everything has just continued to improve. Canada was well bid overnight and the bills have rallied," said a T-bill dealer with one bank-owned brokerage.
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.03 percent from 3.04 percent at Tuesday's close.

Canadian T-bills rallied with the currency on Tuesday after the Fed announced its decision to hold rates steady. Analysts said there had been concern a U.S. rate hike would put downward pressure on the unit. The Canadian dollar strengthened further overnight, reaching C$1.3626 (US$0.7338).
The dealer said trading was active in the Canadian money market this morning.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.35 percent from 3.38 percent. The one-year T-bill firmed to yield 3.68 percent from 3.73 percent at Tuesday's close.
The call loan rate traded at 3.0 percent, the center of the Bank of Canada's 2.75-3.25 percent target range.
